name: Metformin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals; increase by 500 mg weekly or 850 mg every 2 weeks; maximum 2,550 mg/day in divided doses (doses above 2,000 mg may be better tolerated three times daily)
Follow the product's own label (the Glumetza US label: start 500 mg once daily with the evening meal, maximum 2,000 mg once daily)

key_interactions.effect: Lower bicarbonate; higher lactic acidosis risk.
Higher metformin exposure; lactic acidosis risk.
key_interactions.action: Weigh benefits and risks of the combination.

key_interactions.effect: Contrast-related kidney injury can lead to metformin accumulation and lactic acidosis.
key_interactions.action: May need to stop metformin around the procedure (see label 2.3).
Lower insulin or secretagogue doses may be needed.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Drugs that raise glucose (thiazides, corticosteroids, others)
key_interactions.action: Watch glucose when starting or stopping them.

serious: Hypoglycemia with insulin or insulin secretagogues

contraindications: Severe kidney impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2)
Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis
monitoring: eGFR before starting and periodically (at least yearly; more often if at risk)
Hematologic parameters yearly and vitamin B12 every 2 to 3 years (label 5.2)
Hold for iodinated contrast per eGFR rules; recheck eGFR 48 hours after the procedure (label 2.4)

Hold temporarily during acute illness with dehydration, sepsis, hypoxia or acute heart failure, during procedures with restricted food or fluid intake, and for acute kidney injury; restart when eating and kidney function is stable (label 5.1).

pk.bioavailability: About 50% to 60% (500 mg tablet, fasting); food lowers it slightly
pk.peak: About 2 to 3 hours (immediate-release; Tmax 1.8 to 3.3 hours in label Table 4)
pk.half_life: About 6.2 hours in plasma; about 17.6 hours in blood
pk.half_life_eskd: Prolonged; not quantified in the label. Renal clearance about 108 to 130 mL/min at CLcr 10 to 60 vs about 550 to 640 mL/min in healthy adults (label Table 4)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 90% of absorbed drug renally within 24 hours (tubular secretion; renal clearance about 3.5 times CrCl)
pk.dialyzability: Yes: clearance up to 170 mL/min under good hemodynamic conditions (label).
